gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 26?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 26 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

These stable conditions, driven by a weak high-pressure ridge and no strong frontal systems, support the market’s leading implied probabilities for the 27°C (46.5%) and 26°C (32.5%) outcomes. Current runs sit slightly above the long-term August average high of 23.1°C but remain well below historical extremes above 30°C. Updated model guidance and any late adjustments to cloud cover or advection will determine the final official reading used for market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from models like ECMWF and ICON place Munich's August 27 peak temperature near 29–30 °C under a stable high-pressure regime with light easterly flow, partly cloudy skies, and negligible precipitation risk. Minor model spread arises from differences in afternoon cloud cover and boundary-layer mixing, which can shift the daily maximum by 1–2 °C; drier, clearer solutions support 31–32 °C while increased high cloud or slightly stronger winds favor 28–29 °C. Historical late-August climatology in Munich centers around 24–26 °C, so current guidance reflects a modest warm anomaly. Market odds clustered at 30–31 °C reflect this tight consensus amid typical short-range forecast uncertainty.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment for London's highest temperature on August 27 centers on uncertainty in short-range forecast models amid an incoming weather system.** Official guidance from the Met Office and other sources shows a transition from warm, humid conditions on August 25 (highs near 22–24°C) to more unsettled weather, with yellow thunderstorm warnings and spells of heavy rain or showers expected through Thursday.

Key differentiating factors include cloud cover versus sunny intervals, which will determine whether daytime heating reaches 25–26°C or stays capped near 24°C. Easterly or southeasterly winds, high dew points near 17–18°C, and potential for persistent low cloud or precipitation (30–80% chance in some runs) are expected to moderate temperatures. Ensemble forecasts diverge slightly on the timing and intensity of showers, creating the narrow spread between the leading 24°C (33.5%) and 25°C (32.5%) outcomes, while lower probabilities for 26°C or below 24°C reflect the limited upside from Atlantic moisture and the downside risk from widespread cloud.

Upcoming Met Office and ECMWF model updates, plus any observed changes in steering flow, will likely refine these probabilities before resolution.

**Recent official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) and supporting models indicate a transition to cloudier, showery conditions over Tokyo on August 27, moderating peak temperatures relative to the prior hot spell.** 

JMA guidance points to a maximum near 31°C with frequent scattered showers and 50-60% precipitation probability, while other numerical models and outlooks cluster in the 30–33°C range amid high humidity and southerly flow. The primary driver is an approaching low-pressure system and frontal boundary, which increases cloud cover, limits daytime insolation, and introduces evaporative cooling from rain—factors that differentiate the tightly bunched 30–32°C market outcomes. 

Earlier clear, sunny conditions on August 25–26 allowed readings to reach 35°C, but the shift to overcast skies and afternoon/evening thunderstorms is expected to cap the daily high. Minor variations in shower timing, cloud thickness, or model consensus on the low’s track could nudge the outcome by 1–2°C, consistent with the close market-implied probabilities around these levels. Updated JMA briefings and short-range model runs on the morning of the 27th will provide the clearest resolution signals for traders.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 27 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=rjtt

If NOAA data is unavailable or missing for the observation period, Weather Underground will be used as the secondary resolution source.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecasts from authoritative sources like the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), Japan Times, and international models converge on a peak temperature of 33–34°C for Tokyo on August 26, 2026, aligning closely with the market's leading implied probabilities (34°C at 48.5%, 33°C at 25.5%, and 35°C at 21.0%).**

Late-summer conditions in the region feature high humidity, southerly flows, and the urban heat island effect amplifying daytime maxima, while scattered afternoon thunderstorms or increased cloud cover introduce modest cooling potential that caps upside risk. Recent JMA guidance and model runs indicate mainly clear to partly cloudy skies with isolated showers possible later in the day, supporting a most-likely high near 34°C (roughly 93°F). Historical climatology for late August shows typical peaks around 30–32°C, so current conditions reflect above-average warmth without extreme heatwave dynamics. 

Traders appear to weight the consensus central tendency from official forecasts most heavily, with smaller probabilities on 35°C reflecting residual model spread and the chance of clearer conditions allowing an extra degree or two. Resolution will depend on the official JMA daily maximum recorded at the Tokyo station.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and observations point to a peak temperature of 33–34°C in Tokyo on August 26, 2026, consistent with the market’s leading implied probabilities for those outcomes.** Late-summer conditions feature southerly flow and high humidity, but increasing afternoon cloud cover and scattered thunderstorm chances—per Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and international models—are expected to limit extreme heating. Official forecasts cluster between 33°C and 35°C, with several sources highlighting a most-likely high near 34°C (roughly 93°F). Real-time observations mid-morning already reached the low 30s°C, supporting further afternoon rises before any convective cooling.  

The tight clustering around 33–34°C reflects model consensus on modest intensification potential amid the urban heat island effect, while the lower probability for 35°C or higher accounts for rain-cooled air masses that could shave a degree or two from the peak. Historical late-August averages near 30–31°C provide context, but current synoptic patterns favor slightly above-normal readings without the clear skies needed for stronger extremes. Updated model runs and official JMA briefings through the afternoon will be key data points for any final shifts in trader positioning before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus centers on 26–27°C as the most probable peak temperature for Munich today, August 26, 2026, reflecting current forecast guidance from multiple models.** 

Forecasts from sources including the Met Office, WeatherBug, and others consistently indicate a daytime high of 26–27°C (roughly 79–80°F) under partly cloudy skies with light easterly or northeasterly winds, low precipitation chances (around 15–22%), and morning starts in the low teens Celsius. This aligns closely with the market-implied odds favoring 27°C (50%) and 26°C (34.5%), while 28°C holds only modest probability at 10.5%. 

Late August climatology for Munich shows an average high near 23°C, so today’s slightly above-average warmth stems from stable high-pressure influences and reduced cloud cover allowing typical solar heating. Early observations at Munich International Airport report cool dawn temperatures around 12–14°C with high humidity and patchy fog, consistent with rapid afternoon warming to the expected range. No major model disagreements or sudden synoptic shifts (such as stronger advection or thunderstorms) have appeared in recent updates, keeping the distribution tightly clustered around these two outcomes. 

Upcoming hourly observations and the official DWD peak reading will determine resolution, with traders weighting the latest ensemble guidance that shows minimal upside beyond 28°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Met Office and ensemble models indicate a peak around 24–25°C in London on August 27, driven by an incoming low-pressure system and associated cloud cover that limits solar heating. Thunderstorms and heavy rain expected through the morning and early afternoon will enhance evaporative cooling and reduce insolation, while southerly flow brings mild but humid air without strong warm advection. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official and model sources positions 26–27°C as the most probable peak for Munich on August 26, 2026, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes (combined ~84.5% implied probability).** 

German Weather Service (DWD) guidance and high-resolution runs from GFS/ECMWF indicate a partly cloudy day with light easterly to northeasterly flow, allowing modest diurnal heating from a morning low near 12–14°C. Afternoon insolation under broken cloud cover supports a maximum near 25–26°C at standard observation sites, with some ensemble members reaching 27°C if clearing is more extensive. 

This sits modestly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 23.1°C but well below recent early-August peaks and the all-time August 26 record of 35.8°C. Stable synoptic conditions—no strong advection of warmer air or significant moisture—limit upside risk, while residual morning cloud and light winds cap rapid warming, explaining the tight clustering around 26–27°C and the low probabilities assigned to 28°C or higher. 

Traders are effectively pricing the latest model consensus and observed trends from nearby stations, with resolution likely based on the official DWD maximum at Munich-Flughafen or the city station.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official and model sources positions 26–27°C as the most probable peak for Munich on August 26, 2026, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes (combined ~84.5% implied probability).** 

German Weather Service (DWD) guidance and high-resolution runs from GFS/ECMWF indicate a partly cloudy day with light easterly to northeasterly flow, allowing modest diurnal heating from a morning low near 12–14°C. Afternoon insolation under broken cloud cover supports a maximum near 25–26°C at standard observation sites, with some ensemble members reaching 27°C if clearing is more extensive. 

This sits modestly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of 23.1°C but well below recent early-August peaks and the all-time August 26 record of 35.8°C. Stable synoptic conditions—no strong advection of warmer air or significant moisture—limit upside risk, while residual morning cloud and light winds cap rapid warming, explaining the tight clustering around 26–27°C and the low probabilities assigned to 28°C or higher. 

Traders are effectively pricing the latest model consensus and observed trends from nearby stations, with resolution likely based on the official DWD maximum at Munich-Flughafen or the city station.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent official forecasts and observations position 34°C as the consensus outcome for Tokyo’s daily maximum on August 26, 2026.** Multiple sources, including Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) guidance and international models, project a high of 33–34°C under mainly clear to partly cloudy skies with southerly flow and a low-to-moderate chance of afternoon thunderstorms. This aligns with the market’s heavy weighting toward 34°C (63%) and secondary support for 35°C (20.5%) and 33°C (17%).

Late-August climatology in the Tokyo region features a persistent subtropical ridge that advects warm, humid air northward, amplified by the urban heat island effect and typically producing afternoon highs of 31–34°C. Current conditions—surface temperatures already near 32–33°C midday with dew points in the mid-20s—support further diurnal heating into the mid-30s before any convective cooling or increased cloud cover develops. Model consensus shows limited spread, with only modest potential for a 35°C spike if skies remain clearer longer than expected or for a 33°C cap if showers arrive earlier.

No major shifts in steering patterns or moisture profiles have occurred in the past 24–48 hours to alter this outlook, keeping the market-implied distribution tightly clustered around the 33–35°C range consistent with verified observational baselines and short-range guidance.

Historical late-August norms sit near 24–26 °C, so this setup represents above-average warmth driven by the persistent anticyclone. Traders’ tight clustering around 30 °C and 31 °C reflects the narrow forecast spread and limited upside potential from additional warming, while lower probabilities for 32 °C+ acknowledge the modest chance of model underestimation or clearing trends. Updated DWD and ECMWF runs overnight will likely refine the final maximum.

Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 30-32°C because model runs show modest sensitivity to exact timing and intensity of precipitation, with any break in clouds potentially allowing brief spikes toward 32°C and heavier rain favoring the lower end near 30°C. Updated JMA guidance and satellite observations over the next 24 hours will refine these thresholds.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency forecasts and ensemble models indicate a high near 31°C for Tokyo on August 27, driven by increased cloud cover and scattered showers (50-70% probability) that reduce surface insolation relative to the clearer, hotter conditions of August 26. This transition from a southwesterly flow to more northerly or easterly patterns limits afternoon heating while maintaining high humidity. Market-implied odds cluster tightly around 30-32°C because model runs show modest sensitivity to exact timing and intensity of precipitation, with any break in clouds potentially allowing brief spikes toward 32°C and heavier rain favoring the lower end near 30°C. Updated JMA guidance and satellite observations over the next 24 hours will refine these thresholds.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official National Weather Service forecasts for August 26, 2026, in New York City (Central Park and surrounding stations) call for sunny skies with a daytime high near 82–83°F.** Light northwest winds shift southwest by afternoon, supporting gradual warming under clear conditions with minimal cloud cover or precipitation. Early morning lows near 66–69°F and dew points in the upper 50s to low 60s indicate moderate humidity that will not strongly suppress the maximum.

This consensus across NWS tabular products, zone forecasts, and model guidance positions 82–83°F as the most probable outcome, aligning with the market's dominant 63.5% implied probability. Adjacent bins (80–81°F at 22% and 84–85°F at 14.5%) capture remaining uncertainty from minor variations in observed peak timing or localized heating. Stable high pressure and the absence of significant cloud-building or frontal activity reduce the chance of outliers below 80°F or above 85°F.

Traders appear to have incorporated the latest morning model runs and observational trends showing temperatures climbing steadily toward the low-to-mid 80s by afternoon, consistent with late-August climatology for the region. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24 hours to alter this positioning.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance points to a 24°C maximum in London on August 27, driven by a slow-moving Atlantic frontal system that has replaced warmer, more humid air with cooler maritime flow and widespread cloud. Persistent overcast skies and scattered showers reduce solar heating while evaporation from rainfall further limits daytime peaks, keeping values near or slightly below seasonal norms. Ensemble model consensus supports this range, though minor timing shifts in the rain band introduce limited upside potential toward 25°C. Trader positioning around 24–25°C as the leading outcomes reflects the balance between confirmed synoptic cooling and residual forecast spread in the final 24-hour model runs ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official Met Office forecasts for London on August 26, 2026, center on a daytime maximum near 25°C amid partly cloudy skies, light showers, and high humidity, positioning this outcome as the market leader at 64.5% implied probability. Regional guidance notes very warm, humid air with potential for brief sunny spells to push peaks to 26–28°C in parts of southeast England, supporting the secondary 26°C share at 25%. Afternoon model runs and surface observations show light southeast winds limiting further intensification, while scattered precipitation and cloud cover introduce modest downside risk toward 24°C. Traders are weighting the latest agency guidance heavily as resolution nears, with any late-day clearing or convective development capable of shifting the exact high within the narrow 25–26°C band.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Latest Met Office guidance positions a 24–25 °C high as the most likely outcome for London on 27 August.** Official forecasts project a daytime maximum of 25 °C under warm, humid air that is offset by widespread cloud, heavy rain, and thunderstorms, preventing stronger insolation and limiting further warming. Ensemble runs and regional models show broad agreement around this range, with only modest upside risk if breaks in cloud allow brief clearing. The unsettled pattern, driven by low pressure tracking northeast from Iberia, aligns with climatological late-August variability while suppressing the higher temperatures that would otherwise develop under settled high pressure. Final resolution hinges on tomorrow’s observations, with any revised model runs or updated warnings the next likely catalyst for odds movement.

**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) point to a maximum of 31°C in Tokyo on August 27, 2026, under cloudy skies with scattered showers and 50% precipitation probability.** Other models show a narrow range centered near 29–32°C, aligning with the market’s closely bunched leading outcomes (31°C at 27.5%, 32°C at 22%, 30°C at 21.5%).

The primary driver is a frontal system extending across eastern Japan that increases cloud cover and shower activity. Persistent clouds reduce incoming solar radiation and evaporative cooling from rain further caps the daily peak, while any breaks in cloudiness or lighter precipitation could allow temperatures to edge higher. Winds remain light and variable, offering little additional mixing or advection of cooler air.

This setup produces modest day-to-day variability typical of late-summer frontal passages, with the exact maximum hinging on the timing and intensity of showers—factors that numerical models resolve differently. Historical August maxima in Tokyo average near 30–31°C, so the current pattern keeps readings close to seasonal norms rather than exceptional heat. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through the evening of August 26 will provide the final refinements before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official Met Office forecasts position a 25°C maximum as the most likely outcome for London on August 27, with hourly guidance showing a peak near 25°C in the early afternoon amid increasing cloud cover, showers, and thunderstorms.** 

These conditions suppress surface heating by limiting solar insolation and enhancing evaporative cooling from precipitation, keeping temperatures aligned with the 24–25°C range that together command over 70% of market-implied probability. Ensemble guidance from models such as ECMWF and GFS supports similar values, consistent with late-August climatology under a weak high-pressure influence giving way to a frontal system. Traders appear to be weighting the latest official runs heavily, as any last-minute model shift toward clearer skies could allow brief excursions to 26°C, while persistent rain would favor the lower end of the distribution. The market resolves on verified observational data tomorrow evening.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office guidance and ensemble models indicate a maximum of 22–23°C in London on August 28, driven by persistent southwesterly flow, extensive cloud cover, and scattered showers that limit insolation and suppress afternoon peaks. These conditions follow a brief warmer spell earlier in the week and reflect typical late-August Atlantic influence, with dew points around 14–15°C and moderate winds of 10–15 mph further moderating surface temperatures. Minor model spread in timing and intensity of showers creates the close contest between the 22°C and 23°C outcomes, while lower-probability higher readings would require unexpected clearing. Updated Met Office and ECMWF runs over the next 48 hours will likely tighten the range ahead of market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) point to a maximum of 31°C in Tokyo on August 27, 2026, under cloudy skies with scattered showers and 50% precipitation probability.** Other models show a narrow range centered near 29–32°C, aligning with the market’s closely bunched leading outcomes (31°C at 27.5%, 32°C at 22%, 30°C at 21.5%).

The primary driver is a frontal system extending across eastern Japan that increases cloud cover and shower activity. Persistent clouds reduce incoming solar radiation and evaporative cooling from rain further caps the daily peak, while any breaks in cloudiness or lighter precipitation could allow temperatures to edge higher. Winds remain light and variable, offering little additional mixing or advection of cooler air.

This setup produces modest day-to-day variability typical of late-summer frontal passages, with the exact maximum hinging on the timing and intensity of showers—factors that numerical models resolve differently. Historical August maxima in Tokyo average near 30–31°C, so the current pattern keeps readings close to seasonal norms rather than exceptional heat. Updated model runs and JMA briefings through the evening of August 26 will provide the final refinements before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from agencies including the Japan Meteorological Agency indicate a frontal passage bringing increased cloud cover and scattered showers to Tokyo on August 28, limiting daytime heating and producing maximum temperatures clustered around 29–32 °C. Recent days saw highs near 33–35 °C under clearer skies, but the shift to overcast, humid conditions with light southerly or variable winds reduces solar insolation and enhances evaporative cooling. Ensemble spreads reflect timing uncertainties in precipitation and boundary-layer moisture, keeping 30 °C and 31 °C as the most probable outcomes at 31.5 % and 25.5 % market-implied odds. Historical late-August climatology for the region shows similar variability around a 30.3 °C normal high. Updated model runs and observational data over the next 48 hours will refine these probabilities ahead of market resolution.
